rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Solids expand on heating according to $\Delta L = \alpha L \Delta T$, where the **coefficient of linear expansion** α (K⁻¹) is the fractional length increase per degree (NEB 2019, 2022 definitions). It is measured by fixing one end of a rod and reading the tiny extension at the other with a micrometer screw or optical lever while the temperature rises by ΔT.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **α's unit is K⁻¹**, not K — it is per-degree fractional change.  ·  **Clocks lose time in summer** because longer pendulum → longer period → slower ticking.

rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A brass rod 80 cm long at 15 °C is heated to 75 °C (α = 1.9×10⁻⁵ K⁻¹). Find ΔL.** — ΔL = 1.9×10⁻⁵ × 0.8 × 60 = 9.12×10⁻⁴ m ≈ 0.91 mm.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **One coefficient, three expansions:** α (linear), β = 2α (superficial), γ = 3α (cubical).

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: $\Delta L = \alpha L \Delta T$; α in K⁻¹; steel 12×10⁻⁶.  ·  Clock: T = 2π√(L/g) grows with L — summer slow.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Invar (α ≈ 1.2×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹) is used for pendulum rods and precision instruments because it barely expands.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Solids Grow When Warm Railway tracks buckle in summer, bridges have toothed expansion joints, and a pendulum clock keeps different time in winter and summer. All trace to one simple law: a solid's length grows in proportion to its original length and its temperature rise.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2019, 2021, 2022, 2024) ### 2.1 Coefficient of linear expansion **Definition:** the fractional increase in length per degree rise in temperature: $$\alpha = \frac{\Delta L / L}{\Delta T} \Rightarrow \Delta L = \alpha L \Delta T, \quad L_T = L_0(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$$ **SI unit: K⁻¹** (or °C⁻¹ — the same size interval).…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 47:** $\beta = 2\alpha$ (superficial), $\gamma = 3\alpha$ (cubical) — one coefficient generates all three. - **To SHM/pendulum:** period depends on length — thermal expansion perturbs timekeeping. - **To engineering:** expansion joints, bimetallic strips (thermostats), gaps in rails.
